# On-call handoff — gateway 503s

**Status:** unresolved at end of log. Rollback not yet performed.

⚠️ Log timestamps are **2026-03-14**. Today is 2026-08-19. Confirm you're looking at a live incident and not an archived file before you act on any of this.

---

## Root cause

Config generation 119, shipped by **dep-4471**, flipped one key:

```
gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true
```

Each request now takes its own connection from the pool instead of sharing. The pool is 20. Connection opens jumped to ~100x baseline:

```
03:02:30 WARN pool  connection churn: 4180 opens in the last 5m, baseline is 40
```

The pool saturates and never drains. Every request that can't get a connection inside the timeout returns 503.

```
ERROR access  req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms
ERROR pool    req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool
                        (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)
```

Two supporting facts, both pointing at the gateway rather than any backend:

- 503s are split evenly across all four upstreams — accounts 133, billing 132, catalog 133, orders 132. A sick backend would show one number, not four equal ones.
- Pool goes `in_use=20 idle=0` at 02:15 and stays there for the rest of the log. Before 02:14 it never exceeded 11.

The second key in that same change, `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 -> 2500`, is not the cause but makes each failure slower to give up. Roll it back with the rest.

---

## Impact window

| | |
|---|---|
| **Start** | 2026-03-14 **02:14:18** UTC (first 503) |
| **End** | ongoing — log ends 03:59:27, still failing |
| **Duration** | **1h 45m** and counting |
| **Detected** | 03:21:05 — **1h 06m** after onset |

**Blast radius.** All five customer endpoints, equally:

```
/v1/cart             106
/v1/catalog/search   106
/v1/checkout         106
/v1/orders           106
/v1/session          106
```

530 total 503s, latency 600–999ms. Peak wait queue 271 requests deep. On-call page recorded `error_rate 5m avg is 71%`.

**Two things that will bite you:**

1. **`/health` never failed.** After 02:14 the only 200s in the log are health checks — 106 of them, zero real traffic. Health checks use a separate path that doesn't hit the saturated pool. That's why nothing auto-rolled back and why detection took 66 minutes. Fix the health check to exercise the pool.
2. **This log is `node-3 of 3`.** You are looking at one machine. Assume all three, and multiply the numbers by three, until you've checked the other two.

---

## Roll back

### → `dep-4471` (gateway, a.novak, 02:12–02:14)

> *config: connection-per-request for pool isolation*

Revert config **generation 119 → 118**. Minimum viable fix is the single key `gateway.pool.perRequest` back to `false`; a full generation revert also restores `upstreamMs` to 2000.

Timeline that pins it — 4 seconds from deploy finishing to first symptom:

```
02:12:00  dep-4471 starts
02:12:12  reload requested, generation 118 -> 119
02:13:41  generation 119 applied
02:14:00  dep-4471 finishes
02:14:14  first slow-acquire warning
02:14:18  first 503
```

It's also the only config change in the entire log.

**After rollback,** confirm `pool stats` shows `idle > 0` and `waiting=0`, and that non-`/health` requests return 200. The wait queue reset once on its own around 03:13 (271 → 12) with no restart logged — don't read a similar drop as recovery. Only real traffic succeeding counts.

### Do not roll back

- **dep-4472** (billing-svc, 02:41) — shipped 27 min *after* onset
- **dep-4473** (catalog-svc, 03:20) — shipped 66 min after onset

Both land mid-incident and look suspicious. Neither changes anything in the log: same error rate, same slow-acquire progression straight through both windows. The even 4-way upstream split rules out both.

---

## Separate issue — not this incident, don't chase it tonight

`worker.log` shows **zero** errors and zero failed jobs across the same window. Worker DB pool sat at `in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0` all night. Workers talk to the database directly and never touch the gateway, so they were untouched.

But worker job durations climb linearly the whole time — 327ms at 01:00 to 2,197ms at 03:50, exactly +110ms per 10 minutes, no inflection at 02:14. It's already running when the log opens. `db_wait` stays flat at 5ms, and all six job types degrade by the identical 3.19x, which rules out dep-4470's webhook change. A straight line with no queue behind it suggests something accumulating in memory rather than contention.

**File it, don't fix it now.** Unrelated to the 503s.
